definition: A decoding parameter that sharpens or flattens the token probability distribution, controlling randomness.
details: A low temperature makes the most probable tokens even more likely, producing repetitive, focused text; a high temperature flattens the distribution for more varied and creative output. Temperature is one of several sampling controls (with top-k and nucleus/top-p) studied for improving the quality of open-ended neural text generation.

explainer.lead: Temperature is a decoding parameter that sharpens or flattens the token probability distribution, controlling randomness in generation. It matters because it directly trades off focused, repetitive text against varied, creative output.

tiers.eli5: It is a randomness dial: turn it down and the model keeps picking the most likely word; turn it up and it takes more chances.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers set a low temperature for focused, repetitive output and a high one for varied, creative text, often alongside top-k and nucleus/top-p sampling. A pitfall is treating it as the only sampling control, when it is one of several studied for open-ended neural text generation.
tiers.paperLevel: A decoding parameter applied to the token probability distribution: low temperature makes the most probable tokens even more likely; high temperature flattens the distribution. It is one of several sampling controls, with top-k and nucleus/top-p, studied for improving open-ended neural text generation quality.

explainer.example: With a low temperature a model keeps emitting its most probable token; raising the temperature flattens the distribution so less probable tokens can be chosen.

citation.title: The Curious Case of Neural Text Degeneration
